reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm target engagement for any of the three compounds (ipilimumab, nivolumab, cabozantinib). Cannot assess whether CTLA-4, PD-1, or VEGFR2/MET/KIT were adequately engaged. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess whether checkpoint blockade or kinase inhibition pathways were activated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The trial was terminated early with only 4 patients enrolled. Primary endpoint (PFS) shows 6.24 months median but no p-value or comparator data to assess efficacy. The trial was withdrawn due to lack of sponsor support from BMS, not for safety or efficacy reasons. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis possible with only 4 patients. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This appears to be a commercial decision rather than a scientific failure. The trial was underpowered (N=4) and terminated early due to withdrawn sponsor support, not due to safety or efficacy concerns. High rate of serious immune-related AEs (50% grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs) but this is expected for checkpoint inhibitor combinations and doesn't appear to be dose-limiting given the small sample.
